text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — SFO POP egress oscillation detected. Multiple CDN edge sessions reporting elevated RTOs and 5xxs. Impact: partial traffic loss from SFO to certain ISPs. Alert threshold breached (p95 latency + packet loss).

Alex Thompson: seeing 5xx spikes on the CDN dashboard for sfo-pop egress ASNs. RTT to some CDNs jumps to 600ms intermittently.

Maria Chen: confirmed from observability — backend request failures for clients routed via sfo-pop-eu-exit are up 18% last 5m.

Rajiv Patel: oncall network here, looking. Any quick traceroute/tcpdump?

Jessica Ng: running tcpdump on sfo-edge1 now, attaching snip:

```
16:23:40.123456 IP 10.10.1.12.443 > 172.18.5.90.53214: Flags [.], seq 1:141, ack 1, win 229, length 140
16:23:40.124000 IP 10.10.1.12 > 172.18.5.90: icmp 10.10.1.12 unreachable
... repeated icmp unreachables for same flows every ~200ms ...
```

Luke Morrison: got intermittent ICMP unreachable from upstream provider at the MPLS egress. BGP looks flappy for a subset of prefixes.

Rajiv Patel: pulling BGP state from router:

```
# show ip bgp neighbors 203.0.113.2 advertised
Neighbor 203.0.113.2 (external): State: Established
Prefixes received: 12, flaps: 6 in last 10m
Best path changed 8 times
Community: 65001:100
```

Alex Thompson: hmm flaps correlate with customer 5xx windows. Could be MPLS egress path oscillation between two PE routers.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1905-sfo-mpls-egress. Severity: P1. Paging network oncall and SRE.

Maria Chen: @Rajiv do we have a quick mitigation? Can we shift traffic to another POP or set community to prefer alternate egress?

Rajiv Patel: immediate mitigation plan: 1) withdraw problematic routes toward 203.0.113.0/24 via PE-3, 2) advertise more-specifics to force alternate egress, 3) coordinate with provider NOC for MPLS circuit check. I'll do 1 and 2 now.

Jessica Ng: can we also sigma-fanout traffic to ORD POP as fallback for critical customers? We'll need to update route filters in global edge.

Luke Morrison: I can push temporary route policy to favor ord-pop for affected ASNs (ASN 64500, 64510). Applying now.

Alex Thompson: status page draft (short) — "We are investigating elevated errors and latency for traffic through our SFO edge POP. Engineers are mitigating and routing traffic to alternate paths. Some customers may see intermittent failures." Any objections?

Maria Chen: go ahead and post — include ETA for follow-up in 30m.

cdn-ops-bot: Notifying CDN vendor NOC with traceroute samples and BGP timestamps. Ticket #CDN-7891 opened.

Rajiv Patel: executing withdraw on PE-3 for suspect prefixes: `bgp withdraw 203.0.113.0/24`

Jessica Ng: confirmation — traffic to affected CDNs drops immediately but latencies to others improve. Errors on SFO edge down from 18% to 5% in 3m.

Luke Morrison: route policy applied to steer ASN 64500 -> ORD. BGP convergence in progress.

Alex Thompson: good. Start collecting customer impact list: which customers had failed requests routed through SFO last 1h? Maria can we pull from logs?

Maria Chen: running query, pulling top 10 affected customer org_ids. Will paste summary.

```
Affected customers (by observed 5xx count last 60m):
- org_8221: 1200 failures (critical)
- org_9903: 430 failures
- org_7002: 210 failures
- several smaller orgs < 50 failures
```

Rajiv Patel: provider NOC responded — "we see high interface errors on PE-3 towards PE-7, cause unknown, investigating physical interface flaps." They've opened ticket PR-4532.

Jessica Ng: for now ORD failover looks stable. SFO error rate trending down to baseline over last 6m.

incident-bot: Update: severity remains P1 until all prefixes stable for 30m and customer error rates normal.

Alex Thompson: coordinate customer comms: notify org_8221 & org_9903 immediately with targeted note and offer extended logs. @Maria can you run per-org request replay logs?

Maria Chen: started log capture & export for those orgs. ETA 25m.

Rajiv Patel: provider says they replaced a transceiver on PE-3 and observed interface error drop. We'll keep the withdraw in place for another 15m to ensure stability, then we'll reannounce gradually.

Luke Morrison: planning controlled reannounce: reintroduce prefixes with local-preference lower, monitor for flaps for 10m, then restore normal preference. I'll script the policy.

Jessica Ng: monitoring: CDN 5xxs for sfo path down to 2% now. ORD path healthy.

Alex Thompson: good work. Next steps and postmortem owners — Rajiv and Jessica will co-own network portion; Maria + Alex will own customer impact and comms. Postmortem due EOD tomorrow.

Rajiv Patel: will keep watch and hand off to next oncall at 1905003200. If stable after reannounce and 30m quiet, we de-escalate.

incident-bot: Hand-off: @Rajiv -> @Luke at 1905003200 scheduled.

Alex Thompson: adding final note — we've asked provider for root cause analysis and log dumps. Also requesting last-mile ISP telemetry from CDN vendor.

Jessica Ng: leaving detailed snippets for postmortem: sample tcpdump, bgp state, and timeline.

Rajiv Patel: marking this thread as active incident thread. Will update in 5m. :thumbsup:

Luke Morrison: acknowledged, will monitor dashboards and BGP.

incident-bot: Last logged action at 1905002365: controlled withdraw, ORD failover applied, provider hardware swap reported. Monitoring continues.
